meta.scene_summary: We are building the future with one hand and leaving the keys in the ignition with the other.

cooking.headline: DoorDash is buying Instacart to ensure your groceries arrive with a side of cold fries
cooking.summary: The delivery giant is absorbing its grocery counterpart, creating a final boss of unnecessary convenience fees. It is the ultimate consolidation of companies that specialize in charging you double for an apple.
cooking.plain_english: DoorDash has reached an agreement to purchase the grocery delivery service Instacart.

cooking.headline: Google is officially more than just a search bar with a homepage
cooking.summary: Alphabet is finally generating more revenue from things that aren't Blue Links, proving they can make money even when people stop Googling how to fix their code. It turns out the rest of the company is finally doing its homework.
cooking.plain_english: Google's parent company, Alphabet, now generates the majority of its income from services other than its primary search engine.

cooking.headline: Mistral just dropped their heavy artillery into the open weights pool
cooking.summary: Mistral released the weights for their latest Large model, effectively handing the keys to the kingdom to anyone with enough VRAM. It's like the smartest kid in class finally decided to share their notes right before the final exam.
cooking.plain_english: Mistral has publicly released the underlying data for its latest large artificial intelligence model, allowing developers to download and use it for their own projects.

cooking.headline: Nvidia's Grace Blackwell chips are basically a Tetris masterclass
cooking.summary: New scheduling tech is squeezing 27% more performance out of the same hardware by better arranging the workload. It turns out even multi-billion dollar GPUs suffer from the same 'messy roommate' problem where everything just needs to be organized better.
cooking.plain_english: Researchers have developed a new scheduling method that increases the efficiency of Nvidia's Grace Blackwell chips by 27% without needing additional hardware.

cooking.headline: GitHub is basically the world's largest digital hoarding project
cooking.summary: GitHub processed 7.4 billion commits in September, requiring a massive infrastructure upgrade just to keep the lights on. It's comforting to know that even with all that hardware, we're still mostly just pushing 'fixed typo' commits to main.
cooking.plain_english: GitHub processed 7.4 billion code commits in September, which required adding 4 million CPU cores and 160 petabytes of storage to its infrastructure.

cooking.headline: Edge browser security is held together by logic bugs and a prayer
cooking.summary: Researchers chained together a series of logic bugs to bypass Edge's security, proving that complex software is just a house of cards waiting for a breeze. It's comforting to know that even with top-tier security, your browser is basically just a group project where nobody checked the edge cases.
cooking.plain_english: Security researchers successfully demonstrated a full exploit chain against the Microsoft Edge browser using only logical errors in the software code.

cooked.headline: GitLab's security incident is the digital equivalent of leaving the keys in the ignition
cooked.summary: Someone tried to exploit a vulnerability in GitLab, reminding us all that even the most secure dev environments have a screen door. It turns out the only thing harder than writing secure code is realizing everyone else is trying to break it.
cooked.plain_english: GitLab experienced a security incident involving an attempted exploitation of a specific software vulnerability.

cooked.headline: The Department of Homeland Security just leaked their own secret guest list
cooked.summary: The agency responsible for national security managed to leave the door unlocked for 41,000 employees, including the people whose entire job is to stay hidden. It turns out that 'top secret' is just a suggestion when your database permissions are set to public.
cooked.plain_english: A data breach at the Department of Homeland Security exposed the personal information of 41,000 employees, including undercover officers.

cooked.headline: PHP is still the gift that keeps on giving, especially to hackers
cooked.summary: A chained exploit has successfully rooted 25 servers, proving that legacy code is just a ticking time bomb waiting for a creative developer to find the fuse. If you're still running unpatched PHP, you aren't just hosting a website—you're hosting a public access point for the entire internet.
cooked.plain_english: A series of vulnerabilities in PHP has been used to gain unauthorized administrative access to 25 servers, including some belonging to the U.S.

cooked.headline: Android's latest silent update is a zero-click brick button
cooked.summary: Your phone can now be remotely DoS'd without you even touching it, which is the ultimate 'do not disturb' mode. It is the digital equivalent of a coworker cutting your internet cable just to see if you're actually working.
cooked.plain_english: A security vulnerability allows attackers to remotely disable Android devices without requiring any user interaction.
